title: Core team coalesces around bird species/multispecies group
description: Interested parties who will provide leadership come together to create working group

title: Named working group established with defined leadership
description: Working group formed with at least initial leadership responsibilities assigned

title: Human dimensions & biological experts invited to partnership
description: Invitations to multiple spheres of expertise: biologists, ecologists, social scientists, government, habitat managers; core sphere = active working group members, supporting sphere = ancillary members/occasional experts

title: Attention to diversity and inclusivity in core and supporting teams
description: International leaders & groups invited (e.g. Global South co-leads for US/Canada teams); diverse and nontraditional partners invited (amplifies level 3)

title: Group organizational plan and clear rules of engagement established
description: Rules of engagement reflect values on inclusiveness and a clear process for decision making

title: Basic internal communications plan established
description: Email lists, listserv strategies, periodic newsletter?

title: Meeting schedule identified and sustained
description: Group and subgroups meet virtually and/or in person—and continue to meet—on a regular schedule

title: External communication: established website and/or newsletter
description: Structure to maintain group visibility with other working groups and general public (if desired)

title: Multilingual capacity
description: Mechanism in place for translating website, communications, meetings, etc. into English, Spanish, French, or Portuguese (as needed)

title: Strategy for sustaining partnership involvement
description: Strategy in place for ensuring that partner contact and capacity building continue to occur (results of this planning actualized in criteria 1.3.4 and 1.3.5)

title: Organizational and conservation workplan delineating necessary tasks
description: Core team cannot do all the work; workplan articulates necessary tasks and the organization necessary to get tasks done

title: Responsibility for tasks assumed by subcommittees with leaders
description: Permanent or as-needed subcommittees operational with leadership/coordination responsibility clearly designated

title: Subcommittees/local groups deliberately linked horizontally and vertically
description: Flow of information and support between groups/committees is encouraged; all groups linked to larger effort, information transmitted to subgroups and subgroup accomplishments scaled up

title: Intentional capacity building
description: Network implements its plans for sustaining conservation action—continued education, training opportunities, monitoring.

title: Network relationships engender continued conservation action
description: Network strength fosters relationships that lead to autonomous support and conservation action (similar to 6.3.5, but with organizational as opposed to implementation context)

title: Global population size, short-term & long-term trends estimated
description: Some idea of population parameters from isolated surveys and/or expert opinion

title: Global population size, short-term & long-term trends known
description: Greater certainty with respect to population size and trends based on statistically significant survey assessments

title: ACAD Watch List and Tipping Point assessment complete
description: Incorporates breeding & nonbreeding threat level, distribution, and climate change, as well as population size and trend

title: Vulnerability recognized at national, state/province, or partner scales
description: Compilation of national (including Middle/South America), state/province/department, and implementing partner (e.g. Joint Venture, ProAlas, IBA) listings completed

title: Local knowledge included in vulnerability assessment
description: Traditional ecological knowledge as well as unpublished Global South studies and knowledge incorporated in assessment

title: Subspecies identified
description: Known subspecies as described in the literature and museum specimens (may not be relevant for some species)

title: Genoscape analysis completed
description: Genoscape analysis (cf. https://www.birdgenoscape.org/) completed; may not be relevant for all species

title: Spatially explicit population density and trends available
description: Spatially explicit source information in eBird, BBS, ACAD, MoSI, etc.

title: "Natural" populations defined by similar trend trajectories
description: Demographic attributes from long-term monitoring data used to delineate natural population structure (sensu Rushing et al. 2016)

title: Potential partners identified in key breeding geographies
description: Analysis of partnering opportunities in areas of high species density and/or negative population trajectories where conservation action is likely required

title: Migratory status, breeding and nonbreeding geographies identified
description: Source information in eBird, BBS, MoSI, ACAD, Birds of the World

title: Migratory connectivity and migration pathways identified
description: Results of studies of individual birds using isotopes, banding data, geolocators, nanotags, GPS transmitters, etc.

title: Critical migratory stopover locations identified
description: Concentration areas during migration along shorelines, molt migration locations, etc.

title: Linked breeding/nonbreeding areas for declining populations
description: Linkages established between distinctly declining breeding populations and nonbreeding areas for the same populations

title: Potential partners contacted in key nonbreeding geographies
description: Linkages established with biologists, ecologists, ornithologists, sociologists, conservationists, etc. in linked geographies of interest

title: Spatially explicit breeding season success, breeding productivity known
description: In addition to trends, actual spatially explicit breeding vital rates have been identified (e.g., nest success, production, fledgling survival)

title: Nonbreeding and annual cycle vital rates known
description: Adult survival during breeding and nonbreeding seasons, first year survival, dispersal, recurrent migratory mortality

title: Ecological and life history correlates of vital rates identified
description: Age- and sex-specific demographic and life history differences have been identified and quantitatively estimated

title: Integrated population model (IPM) completed
description: Full IPM model, or a determination that inference is sufficient to proceed with conservation action with incomplete knowledge

title: Socioeconomic correlates of demographic parameters identified
description: E.g., are spatially explicit vital rates correlated with land ownership, conservation policies, or management practices?

title: Demographically linked populations identified
description: Demographic analyses corroborate and refine linked migratory populations suggested by 2.3.4 assessment

title: IPM and linked population geography used to identify focus areas
description: When in the annual cycle and where in the species range would conservation action most likely change population trajectory?

title: Partnering opportunities identified in focus areas
description: In biologically assessed focal areas, partnership landscape assessed (e.g., private or public lands; economic status of local communities)

title: Key partner opportunities refined and contacts established
description: Network analysis suggests partnerships (not just bird-oriented) that might be most promising for leveraging conservation action

title: Biological focus areas refined by including human landscape assessment
description: Biological and social dimensions combined to further refine areas in which to focus species conservation actions

title: Review of published knowledge relevant for identified focus areas
description: In addition to target species studies, what can we learn about focus areas that would be important (e.g. climate change, human well-being issues)?

title: Review of relevant local knowledge, published or unpublished
description: Thorough attempt to include studies published in Global South, unpublished reports, insights from scientists working in focus areas

title: Local community contacts identified in focus areas
description: Leaders of 3.2.4 partnerships identified (e.g., tribal biologists, community action leaders, strong links from amplified social network analysis)

title: Local and Traditional Ecological Knowledge assessed
description: Conversations with above community leaders results in inclusion of local insights and indigenous Traditional Ecological Knowledge

title: Focus area profile completed
description: Synthesis of social, biological, geopolitical, and traditional ecological knowledge for focus areas

title: Breeding habitat and ecology known
description: Detailed breeding and foraging habitat relationships, including  breeding system, brood sequence, nest sites, foraging niche, diet, etc., needed to identify specific threats

title: Nonbreeding habitat and ecology known
description: Nonbreeding habitat relationships, including dispersal, migration, interspecies relationships, foraging niche, molt requirements, etc., needed to identify specific threats

title: Spatially explicit habitat mapping, breeding and nonbreeding
description: GIS mapping of available and restorable habitat, breeding and nonbreeding, especially within focus areas

title: Human activities affecting breeding habitat quality identified
description: What are the most important anthropogenic factors affecting breeding habitat quality at habitat (not regional) scale?

title: Human activities affecting nonbreeding habitat quality identified
description: What are the most important anthropogenic factors affecting nonbreeding habitat quality at habitat (not regional) scale?

title: Broad regional breeding season threats identified
description: Broad (e.g., agriculture, urbanization) regionally specific threats identified (using, e.g., Conservation Standards, Audubon threats map)

title: Broad regional nonbreeding season threats identified
description: Broad (e.g., conversion to pasture) regionally specific threats identified for nonbreeding season, including local knowledge

title: Socioeconomic drivers of threats identified
description: Preliminary analysis of anthropogenic drivers of threats, including assessment of societal value and social perceptions of threats

title: Systematic threats analysis, refinement, and prioritization
description: Threats prioritization (e.g., Conservation Standards) also includes feasibility based on human dimensions assessment

title: Existing campaigns for addressing priority threats identified
description: Analysis of partnering opportunities (allies) for addressing threats, especially in areas of high species density and/or negative population trajectories

title: Threat analysis applied to focus areas
description: Analysis of links between IPM model (where/when), focus area determination (3.3.5), and identified threats

title: Intersection between species ecology and threats explored
description: Intersection of broad threat and species ecology allows refinement of threat to level of a limiting factor hypothesis (e.g., wood encroachment removal from nonbreeding season grasslands)

title: Socioeconomic analysis of hypothetical limiting factor
description: Identification of anthropogenic drivers underlying limiting factor (e.g., what are the social aspects leading to woody encroachment in nonbreeding season grasslands?)

title: Local or Traditional Ecological Knowledge included
description: Full incorporation of additional local knowledge in identifying specific limiting factor to be addressed

title: Species-specific limiting factor(s) identified
description: Limiting factor identified and refined at scale sufficient to design adaptive research or initiate targeted conservation action (e.g., wood encroachment removal from nonbreeding season grasslands)

title: Prioritize alignment with broad-scale threat reduction campaigns
description: From allied partner opportunity analysis (4.2.5), prioritize existing broadscale efforts most compatible with meeting species-specific needs (breeding and/or nonbreeding)

title: Identify compatible allied partnership goals and objectives
description: Listen carefully, understand aligned partner goals and objectives to determine entry points for mutual-benefit strategic planning

title: Identify beneficial practices for working with outside partners
description: Draw from social science expertise on strategies for alignment with partners with different goals and objectives than bird species recovery

title: Develop strategies for aligning bird objectives with allies
description: Identify programs (entry points) most closely aligned with species objectives (e.g., CRP in Food Bill, rotational grazing, dynamic landscape forest harvest planning, etc.)

title: Subcommittee(s) established to influence/work with partner opportunities
description: Create dedicated and intentional structure within working group to continue to develop relationships with allies (e.g., collective representative to lobby policy, presence on forestry councils, etc.)

title: Establish species population goals and objectives
description: How is "recovery" defined? Population goals as either numbers or trends, ideally identified both rangewide and parsed by focus areas

title: Develop influence diagram/results chain to address limiting factor
description: Diagram of chain of events (e.g., Open Standards)—including threats, barriers, actions, and issues—leading to mitigation or elimination of limiting factor(s)

title: Incorporate human well-being objectives into results chain
description: Results chain (cf. Open Standards) includes human well-being or affected community benefits that accrue from conservation actions

title: Determine sequential stages, progress metrics, research & monitoring plan
description: Results chain clearly identifies sequential actions or research, inflection points for adaptive decisions, intermediate and final evaluation metrics

title: Estimate costs required to reach limiting factor mitigation
description: Estimates of the costs of each stage of research/mitigation plan

title: Full annual cycle conservation plan completed
description: Plan includes review of biology and human dimensions profile; threats analysis; limiting factor analysis; research plan; strategies to reduce threats and mitigate limiting factors

title: Full annual cycle conservation investment plan completed
description: As above, but adds cost of investments of recovery phases; plan for scaling up conservation actions; monitoring and evaluation strategy

title: Funding source and partnership analysis completed
description: What agencies, policies, or programs are potential sources of funding for different components of research/recovery conservation plan?

title: Strategy to contact and court funding sources
description: Communication and outreach strategy to secure funding for plan components

title: Funding secured to proceed with conservation plan implementation
description: Plan includes strategy for moving forward under scenarios of partial funding; ideally guided by results chain breakdown in 5.2.4 & 5.2.5

title: Focus area habitat restoration research initiated
description: Habitat management need not be delayed until full plan completion if research is needed to test limiting factor hypotheses

title: Habitat restoration effectiveness confirmed
description: Monitoring confirms effectiveness of habitat restoration (or other local action, e.g. hunting management) as a means of mitigating limiting factor

title: Research/restoration conducted with affected community involvement
description: Full participation of affected community as partners in research and habitat manipulations (or other local actions, e.g. hunting management)

title: Scale of restoration/management strategy expanded
description: Initial success of mitigation strategy suggests expanding strategy to other localities within or outside focus area; cycle 6.1.1 to 6.1.4 repeats

title: Monitoring of both social and bird population outcomes
description: Monitoring continues to confirm success of limiting factor mitigation OR requires adaptive changes that may necessitate revisiting other segments of the wheel

title: Partnership strategies for broad-scale change initiated
description: Broad-scale threat reduction strategies initiated through partnerships with allied campaigns (e.g., grassland protection/restoration, CRP, feral cat control)

title: Monitoring of species population response to broad threat mitigation
description: Are target bird species populations responding positively to broad-scale threat mitigation?

title: Species requirements integrated successfully into ecosystem conservation
description: Based on species population response, do inclusion of species-specific requirements need to be re-negotiated?

title: Monitoring/assessment of species group/allied campaign relationship
description: Social science analysis to evaluate relationship between bird species working group and allies; recommendations for adaptive changes

title: Effective communication of success of ecosystem partnership
description: Continued reinforcement of positive effects of bird species/threats reduction campaign alliance (e.g., flood control, drinking water, human health improvements, etc.)

title: Focus area recovery scaled up to rangewide population recovery
description: Initial success mitigating limiting factors within focus areas scaled up to achieve rangewide population recovery; may require recycling iteratively through wheel criteria

title: Rangewide adaptive monitoring plan in place
description: Long-term monitoring plan designed to detect species vulnerabilities (new limiting factors) and trigger adaptive recovery response

title: Final reporting, documentation, and outreach
description: Documentation of process, barriers and solutions, and successes completed to provide guidance to other species/ecosystem recovery efforts

title: Network and capacity building
description: Attention given throughout recovery process to building local community capacity (biology and sociology training), education for next generation of conservationists

title: Established relationships transcend goals/issues
description: Established individual and community relationships and problem-solving orientation transcend recovery process, can be leveraged for future conservation action
